releases.name: Archive Viewer

cover.alt: A ZIP in Archive Viewer: the file tree with sizes and dates on the left, its README with line numbers and details on the right.

screenshots.alt: src/index.ts from a ZIP with Orca's light theme: the src folder open in the tree, the file with line numbers, compression method, CRC-32 and encoding.
public/hero.png selected in the archive tree with Orca's dark theme, previewed on a checkerboard with its dimensions, 480 × 300.
charts-1.8.2.jar opened from inside the ZIP, with the breadcrumb Archive › charts-1.8.2.jar; BarChart.class shows as hex starting with ca fe ba be.
A .tar.gz filtered by ".ts" with Orca's light theme: the matching files highlighted in their folders, forecast.ts previewed on the right.

releases.changelog:
Added

- Archive Viewer editor for .zip, .jar, .war, .ear, .aar, .apk, .whl, .nupkg,
  .vsix, .xpi, .ipa, .epub, .tar, .gz, .tgz, .bz2, .tbz2, .tbz, .xz,
  .txz, .zst and .tzst; formats are recognised by their bytes, 7-Zip, RAR, lzip, .Z and
  .cab get a clear "not supported" message.
- ZIP: end record search with self-extracting prefixes, ZIP64, data descriptors, Unix modes and
  symlinks, Info-ZIP Unicode paths and extended timestamps, NTFS times; stored, Deflate, bzip2
  and Zstandard entries with a CRC-32 check; encrypted and other methods are named, not unpacked.
- TAR: ustar, GNU long names and links, PAX headers, base-256 sizes, symbolic and hard links;
  GZIP (several members), bzip2, XZ and Zstandard streams, with the tar inside or a single file
  named from the GZIP header, each GZIP member checked against its CRC-32 and size. Unpacking
  stops at 512 MB; archives inside archives open up to 8 levels deep and 1 GB together.
- Clear messages for valid files beyond the decoders' limits: Zstandard windows over 128 MB, XZ
  dictionaries over 64 MB, and XZ with a SHA-256 check or BCJ or delta filters. A damaged or
  cut-off GZIP file shows what could be read with a notice.
- Names without UTF-8 marking in CP437, CP866 (default for a Russian UI) or Windows-1251,
  switchable in the toolbar.
- Virtualized file tree with size, packed and date columns; filter (⌘F / Ctrl+F), expand
  and collapse all, summary with the compression ratio, keyboard navigation.
- Preview: text with line numbers and wrapping, images, hex dump, details (method, date,
  permissions, CRC-32, link target); archives inside archives open in place with a trail back;
  Save… through Orca's save dialog and Copy path. The README is selected on opening.
- English and Russian UI, Orca's light and dark themes, plugin and tab icons.

plugins.description: Browse archives in Orca's editor tabs: .zip, .jar, .apk, .whl, .epub and other ZIP files, .tar, and .gz, .bz2, .xz or .zst (also .tar.gz and friends). A fast file tree with sizes and dates, a filter, previews of the text, images and hex inside, nested archives, legacy code page names and saving single files. Read-only, offline.

releases.name: Class File Viewer

cover.alt: Class File Viewer on a jar: the package tree with Telescope selected, and its declarations in Java syntax with a Java 21 badge.

screenshots.alt: The Bytecode tab on Telescope.point(): stack=4, locals=4, args_size=2, and each constant explained in a comment.
A jar's overview: 84 classes, 9 packages, 1 resource; 83 compiled for Java 21, 1 for Java 8; its module and main class.
The Constant pool tab, 4 Methodrefs: #67 Optics.limitingMagnitude refers to #68 and #69 and is used in observe at offset 12.
The Structure tab: Telescope's class header (6,880 bytes, CA FE BA BE, version 65.0) and the table of its 8 fields.
Units in a multi-release jar, switched from Base to Java 17+: its Java 17 copy, outlined. Shown in Orca's light theme.

releases.changelog:
Added

- .class files open in Class File Viewer by default, with four tabs: **Outline** (the
  declarations in Java syntax, with links to each method's bytecode and, in a jar, to the
  classes it names), **Bytecode** (listed like javap -c -v), **Structure** (the class file's
  header, members and attributes, each with its offset, length and bytes) and **Constant pool**
  (filterable, cross-linked, with what uses each entry).
- A **Java N** badge for the release a class was compiled for, and badges for classes compiled
  by Kotlin (with its @Metadata version in Structure), Scala, Groovy or Clojure.
- .jmod files open by default, and .jar, .war, .ear and .aar files as an option, in a
  browser of packages and classes: nested classes under their outer class, class roots of web
  and Spring Boot archives, multi-release versions, archives inside opened in place, previews
  of resources and an overview with the Java versions of the classes, the module (a .jmod's
  too) and the manifest. Entries are taken as the JVM takes them: the central directory
  java.util.zip reads, by stored name, the last copy winning, and the manifest and version
  folders as Java 21 finds them. Unusual names, shadowed copies and entries named like folders
  that hold data are listed apart, with a notice; so is an archive with a second directory.
- Clear messages for newer, damaged, cut-off and misnamed files and for damaged attributes;
  obfuscated names shown with escapes. Code longer than the JVM allows is shown as damaged, and
  the Bytecode tab lists up to a million instructions and table rows, with a notice past that.
- Find, Copy and Save…; keyboard navigation of the tree.
- English and Russian, following Orca's language; Orca's light and dark themes.

plugins.description: Read compiled .class files in Orca's editor tabs: declarations in Java syntax, bytecode listed like javap, the file's structure and a linked constant pool. Jars, wars, ears, aars and jmods open as a tree of packages and classes. Offline, no JDK needed. Independent; not affiliated with Oracle.

releases.name: Font Viewer

cover.alt: Inter in Font Viewer: sample text, a waterfall of sizes and the alphabets, with the optical size and weight axes and OpenType features on the right.

screenshots.alt: Source Serif 4 at weight 602 with Orca's light theme: sample text, the size waterfall, the Weight and Optical Size sliders and OpenType features.
Inter's Characters tab with Orca's dark theme: a grid of characters with code points, the ampersand selected with its HTML, CSS and JavaScript forms.
The Info tab for Lora with Orca's light theme: names, designer and vendor links, style and metrics, the weight axis and the licence.

releases.changelog:
Added

- **Font Viewer** custom editor for .ttf, .otf, .woff, .woff2, .ttc and .otc: the
  default view for these files, read-only and offline.
- Preview tab: editable sample text (a Russian pangram for a Russian UI when the font has
  Cyrillic, else the font's own sample or an English pangram), size from 8 to 200 px with
  presets, line height, a waterfall of nine sizes and the alphabet lines the font covers.
- Variable fonts: a slider per axis that reaches the axis's exact minimum, maximum and default,
  and the named instances; only the axes you move or an instance sets are applied, so the browser
  keeps its automatic optical size. OpenType feature switches with readable names (stylistic sets
  use the names the font gives them).
- Collections: a face picker; only the chosen face is read in full and drawn on its own, and a
  face that cannot be read is marked in the picker while the others still open.
- Characters tab: every mapped character grouped by Unicode block, drawn only where it is on
  screen, a search by character, U+0416, a U+0400-04FF range or the words of a block name
  (latin-1, box draw, IPA ext), a block filter, arrow-key navigation that keeps its column
  across blocks, and a detail panel with the character large on its baseline and its code
  point as U+, decimal, HTML, CSS, JavaScript and UTF-8, each with a copy button.
- Info tab: names (links open in the browser through Orca), weight, width, metrics, licence,
  embedding rights, format, outlines, file size, glyph and character counts, dates, colour
  formats, problems found while reading (tables cut off by the end of the file, a damaged
  character map skipped for the next one), and the table directory. A font whose head, name
  or cmap is missing or cut off gets a "damaged" message instead of an empty view.
- Font parser for sfnt, collections, WOFF 1.0 (fflate) and WOFF 2.0 (brotli.js), unit-tested on
  fonts built by tools/make-fixtures.py and on damaged and hostile fonts built in the test

plugins.description: Fonts in Orca's editor tabs: opens .ttf, .otf, .woff, .woff2, .ttc and .otc files with sample text at any size, a waterfall of sizes, variable axes and named instances, OpenType feature switches, every character grouped by Unicode block with code points to copy, and the font's names, metrics, licence, embedding rights and tables. Works offline, never edits the file.

releases.name: HAR Viewer

cover.alt: Known secrets masked, 28 values in 15 requests: the request list and waterfall, a failed POST /v1/reports/export selected.

screenshots.alt: A Markdown digest of the 4 failed requests, bodies cut to 2,000 characters and known secrets masked, to copy or save as .md.
The Errors filter keeps 4 of 29 requests, beside an overview of their types, status codes and the 2 domains they came from.
A slow request by phase: DNS 18 ms, connection 42 ms, SSL/TLS 31 ms, waiting 1.20 s, and Server-Timing's report query 1.10 s.
A 2.4 kB JSON response in Tree view, Source a click away: 20 orders, the first opened to its id, customer, total and status.
Follow one order: 4 of 19 socket messages match 48207, sent and received, one opened as JSON. Shown in Orca's light theme.

releases.changelog:
Added

- **HAR Viewer** custom editor, the default view for .har and .har.zip (Archive Viewer, when
  installed, keeps .har.zip and offers HAR Viewer in the view switcher): read-only and
  offline. Reads HAR 1.2 from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, Playwright and agent tools with
  their extra fields, base64 bodies, missing or -1 timings and requests without pages.
- .har.zip from Playwright with bodies in separate files, unpacked in the tab (vendored
  fflate 0.8.3).
- A virtualized request list with sortable columns (status, method, domain, path, type,
  initiator, transferred, size, time) and a waterfall with a time scale and each page's
  DOMContentLoaded and load lines; a resizable split; keyboard navigation.
- Filters: text over the URL, headers or everything including bodies, with negation, phrases,
  regular expressions and properties such as status:5xx or larger-than:100k; type chips;
  errors only; page and domain.
- Details tabs: Headers with raw views, Payload, Response (JSON tree, highlighted source,
  image, font, muted audio and video previews, hex), Cookies, Timing with Server-Timing,
  WebSocket messages and Initiator with the call stack and related requests.
- An overview with totals, requests by type and status, a per-domain table that filters the
  list, and the slowest, largest and failed requests; a summary strip under the list.
- Copy as cURL and as fetch (every value an option's argument; header names that are not tokens
  left out; requests with control characters in the URL, method or headers not copied); "Export for agent", a Markdown digest of selected, failed or
  listed requests with bodies cut and known secret patterns masked, to copy or save.
- "Mask secrets" with a banner counting what was masked, and "Save sanitized…" for a masked
  .har or .har.zip. Masking knows credential headers and cookies (folded and nameless
  ones too), secret-named parameters in URLs, fragments and hash routes, form fields
  (urlencoded, multipart, plain tex

plugins.description: Shows .har and Playwright .har.zip files as a network log: request list, waterfall, filters and each request's headers, payload, response, cookies, timing and WebSocket frames. Copy as cURL, export an agent digest, save a masked copy. Independent; not affiliated with Playwright or any browser maker.

releases.name: Image Viewer

cover.alt: Image Viewer on an OpenEXR render: the Part picker, +0.5 EV exposure and Filmic tone mapping in the toolbar above the image.

screenshots.alt: The Layers tab lists layers and groups with blend mode, opacity and size; the Badge smart object is shown alone at 100%.
A Radiance HDR render at −2.0 EV, Filmic: the lamp keeps its shape, and the pixel readout shows its stored R 16.0625.
A DNG's embedded preview beside its camera and location details: 1/250 s, f/8, ISO 100, 35 mm, 40° 45′ 36″ N, 113° 53′ 24″ W.
A DDS cube map in 16-bit float: the Face and Mip pickers in the toolbar, and a Faces list of all six faces with −Z shown.
A HEIC photo with its details: a 4 × 2 grid of 512 × 512 tiles, codec hvc1.3.E.L90.B0, 8-bit. Shown in Orca's light theme.

releases.changelog:
Added

- Image Viewer, the default editor for .tif, .tiff, .psd, .psb, .exr, .hdr, .pic,
  .tga, .dds, .qoi, .icns, .heic, .heif and .hif, and for the camera RAW files
  .dng, .cr2, .cr3, .nef, .nrw, .arw, .srf, .sr2, .raf, .rw2, .rwl, .orf,
  .ori, .pef, .srw, .iiq, .mos, .erf and .kdc.
- TIFF: pages and reduced-resolution sub-images, strips and tiles, chunky and planar, 1–32-bit
  integers and 16–64-bit floats, LZW, Deflate, PackBits, JPEG and WebP, predictors, RGB, grey,
  palette, CMYK, YCbCr and CIELAB, BigTIFF.
- PSD and PSB: the saved composite, each layer, groups, layer visibility and a composite of the
  visible layers (blend modes, opacity, clipping, masks); layers composited with a notice when the
  file has no composite.
- OpenEXR: scanline and tiled, multi-part, layers, MIP and RIP levels, half/float/uint channels,
  NONE, RLE, ZIPS, ZIP, PIZ, PXR24, B44 and B44A.
- Radiance HDR, TGA (with the 2.0 extension), QOI, and ICNS with every icon size (JPEG 2000
  entries listed as not supported).
- DDS: uncompressed formats, BC1–BC7 including BC6H, MIP levels, cube faces, array layers and
  volume slices.
- HEIC and HEIF: own container reader with grids, rotation, mirroring, cropping, alpha, depth and
  matte images, thumbnails; HEVC and AV1 decoded by the system through WebCodecs, and a plain
  explanation with the file's details where the system has no HEVC decoder.
- Camera RAW: the largest embedded preview and the smaller ones, EXIF, sensor details and maker
  notes for eight makers, the camera name from XMP when the TIFF tags lack it; no RAW development,
  said in a notice.
- Zoom and pan, Fit and 1:1, checkerboard and pixel grid, pixel values under the pointer, image
  pickers in the toolbar, a side-pane list with thumbnails (TIFF pages, PSD layers, EXR parts,
  DDS faces and array layers, ICNS sizes, RAW previews), channel views, histogram, levels and Auto
  contrast for every image, exposure and tone curves for HDR, keyboard shortcuts.
- Details pane:

plugins.description: Image formats Orca can't show, in its editor tabs: TIFF, HEIC and HEIF, PSD and PSB, EXR, HDR, TGA, DDS, QOI, ICNS, and the embedded previews of camera RAW files. Zoom to the pixel, pages, layers and mip levels, HDR exposure, channels, EXIF, XMP and GPS details, Save as PNG. Read-only, offline.

releases.name: Media Viewer

cover.alt: Media Player in an Orca tab: a paused clip of a sunset over hills, with the seek bar, volume, speed, repeat, snapshot, fit, info and full screen controls below.

screenshots.alt: An .mkv video paused at 0:12 in the Media Player tab with Orca's dark theme.
The same video in the Media Player tab with Orca's light theme.
The file info overlay over the video: file, size 1.9 MB, resolution 1920 × 1080, duration 0:30, frame rate, type .mkv.
An audio file in the Media Player: a music note cover above the seek bar at 1:04 of 3:34.

releases.changelog:
Added

- .avi opens in Media Player instead of "Binary file — cannot display". The tab converts it to MP4 offline when it opens (FFmpeg in WebAssembly decodes, the browser's WebCodecs encoders write H.264 or VP9 with Opus or AAC) and shows the progress. Video: Xvid, DivX 3/4/5, MPEG-4, H.264, H.263, MJPEG, MPEG-1/2; sound: MP3, MP2, AC3, AAC, PCM, ADPCM, surround mixed down to stereo. Unsupported codecs and damaged files get a clear message.

Changed

- License is now MIT AND LGPL-2.1-or-later: the bundled FFmpeg decoder (vendor/ffmpeg) is LGPL; its source and build script are in wasm/.

releases.name: Media Viewer
releases.changelog:
Added

- File icon theme "Media Viewer" (Settings → Appearance → Icon theme): video and audio files get their own icons in tabs, the file tree, Quick Open and search, even when Orca's built-in player opens them. It maps only media files; other files show Orca's built-in icons while it is selected.
- Tabs opened in Media Player show a video or an audio icon instead of the plugin icon.

Changed

- Media Player is split into video and audio editors (media, media-audio, media-plus, media-plus-audio) so each gets its tab icon.

releases.name: Media Viewer
releases.changelog:
Added

- Icon, cover and screenshots for the plugin page in Orca and on orca.dev.

Changed

- File info shows "— (measured during playback)" for the frame rate until the clip has played, instead of a guessed "≈ 30 (unknown)".

releases.name: Media Viewer
releases.changelog:
Added

- Media Player for video and audio in Orca's editor tabs, opened from the file tree, chat file links or orca file open.
- Opens .mkv, .mka and .weba by default (Orca has no viewer for them).
- Offered in the tab's view toggle for .mp4, .m4v, .mov, .webm, .mp3, .wav, .m4a, .aac, .ogg, .oga, .flac and .opus, keeping Orca's built-in player as the default.
- Controls: play/pause, seek, volume and mute, speed 0.25×–3×, repeat, frame stepping, fit / actual size, full screen.
- Save the current frame as PNG through Orca's save dialog.
- File info overlay: size, resolution, duration, measured frame rate, type.
- Audio cover in place of a black frame.
- Keyboard shortcuts, light and dark themes, English and Russian UI.

plugins.description: Video and audio in Orca's editor tabs: plays .mkv, .avi, .mka and .weba, which Orca cannot show (AVI is converted offline in the tab), and adds a full player view to .mp4, .mov, .webm, .mp3, .flac and other media. Speed, frame stepping, repeat, frame snapshots, file info and keyboard shortcuts.
